The manual's version, from its DESCRIPTION

Source: R/building.R
manualVersion.Rd

Reads Version and puts it in an environment variable, which is how a manual's index.Rmd gets it onto the title page: the YAML header is parsed before any of the book's code runs, so a subtitle can only reach it through the environment.

Usage

manualVersion(
  description = "DESCRIPTION",
  envVar = "SPADES_MANUAL_VERSION",
  legacy = character(0)
)

Arguments

description

path to the DESCRIPTION file to read.

envVar

name of the environment variable to set.

legacy

additional variable names to set to the same value, for documents that still read a manual-specific name such as LANDR_MAN_VERSION. Empty by default.

Value

the version string, invisibly.

Details

By field name, never by position. A manual that read read.dcf(...)[4] got Version only because it happened to be the fourth field, so adding any field above it would have printed the wrong string on the title page.

A manual whose chapters still read a name of its own passes it as legacy, e.g. manualVersion(legacy = "LANDR_MAN_VERSION"). Nothing is set by default: setting every manual's name in every manual meant each one exported variables belonging to the others.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## in build.R, before render_book()
manualVersion()
} # }
